## What's Changed

### Escalate rules: operations that always go to a human (opt-in)

`reviewer.instructions` are guidance a model may still get wrong. The new top-level `escalate` option lists operations that are escalated to a human **before any reviewer sees them**, with every backend and both plugin API generations. In `on-ask` mode the OpenCode prompt stays; in `all-tools` mode the tool is blocked with the matched rule as the reason.

```jsonc
"options": {
  "escalate": [
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "*git push*" },
    { "action": "webfetch" },
    { "action": "*", "resource": "*.env" }
  ]
}
```

- `action` matches the permission action (`on-ask`) or the tool name (`all-tools`); the shell is `shell` on OpenCode 2.x and `bash` on 1.x.
- `resource` uses OpenCode's `*` / `?` wildcards and is matched against every string value, whole, per line and per shell word, ignoring case and whitespace runs. Matching never uses a regular expression.
- What `write` / `edit` / `multiedit` write is not matched, and an `apply_patch` patch is matched through its file headers, so a path rule does not fire on code that merely mentions a path.
- Inputs too deep or too large to check escalate under any rule for their action.
- Rules are a deterministic floor, not a sandbox: keep OpenCode `deny` permissions for what must never run.

* feat: add deterministic escalate rules by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/75

### Credentials are redacted before review, and reviews in flight are capped

**Behavior change:** by default, the state sent to the reviewer's provider now has credential values replaced by markers such as `[REDACTED]`: the configured `reviewer.decision` / `reviewer.chat` API keys, private key blocks, URL passwords, well-known token formats, and secret-shaped values after `Authorization:` / `Bearer`, `--password` / `--token`-style flags, or in `*_KEY=` / `*_TOKEN=` / `*_SECRET=` / `*_PASSWORD=` assignments. The tool OpenCode runs is never changed. Redaction is deliberately conservative so that crafted text cannot hide a path, host, URL or command from the reviewer. Add patterns with `reviewer.redact.patterns`, or turn it off with `reviewer.redact.enabled: false`.

**Behavior change:** at most `reviewer.maxConcurrentReviews` reviews (default 4, 1–32) run at once. More wait for a free slot for up to `reviewer.timeoutMs` and then escalate.

See [What reviewers receive](https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin#what-reviewers-receive).

* feat: redact credentials and cap concurrent reviews by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/77

### Hardening of the all-tools native-ask grant

- With `allToolsNativeAsks: "review"`, a native ask is only answered when the live tool call still has the same tool and input as the one reviewed. A call whose input changed during review now fails closed in every all-tools mode.
- `allToolsNativeAsks: "review"` is now rejected at startup with `mode: "on-ask"` and on the OpenCode 1.x plugin API, where it does nothing.

* fix: refuse native ask grants for calls rewritten after review by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/70

### Configuration that does nothing is rejected

`reviewer.agent.cleanupSessions` is now rejected at startup on the OpenCode 1.x plugin API and with the SDK runtimes, instead of being silently ignored. Invalid options are reported with an `Invalid auto-approval plugin options:` prefix.

* fix: assert reviewer session cleanup and reject it where it does nothing by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/73

### Security audit follow-ups

- A reviewer reply with too many braces to rule out a conflicting second verdict is no longer trusted, unless it is unambiguous.

## What's Changed

### Let the reviewer answer native asks in all-tools mode (OpenCode V2, opt-in)

In `all-tools` mode, a tool call the reviewer had already approved could still stop at OpenCode's native **Permission required** prompt, for example a subagent's `shell` call under a `shell: ask` rule. The new `allToolsNativeAsks: "review"` option lets the reviewer's approval answer that native ask too.

```jsonc
"options": {
  "mode": "all-tools",
  "allToolsNativeAsks": "review"
}
```

- The default is `"preserve"`, and upgrading does not change behavior: configured native `ask` rules still reach a human. With `"review"` the reviewer answers them instead, including rules you set as human checkpoints such as `"git push *": "ask"`, so enable it only if that is what you want.
- An approval only covers the native ask that matches the reviewed tool, within the same session, agent, message and tool call. It expires after 45 seconds and is revoked when the user prompts the root session again.
- Other native actions raised by the call (for example `external_directory` with its resolved path) get a separate review of their actual resources. A failed or escalated extra review denies the call without prompting.
- Explicit native `deny` rules and AI `deny`/`escalate` verdicts still block the call. V1 is unchanged.
- Input changed by a later hook is only detected after the tool runs, so this is not a hard boundary. Use it only with plugins and hooks you trust.

* fix: honor AI all-tools approvals during native permission checks by @thisfilipe in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/53

### Codex reviewer ignores the workspace's `.codex/config.toml`

With `reviewer.agent.runtime: "codex-sdk"`, Codex runs in the reviewed project. If you had trusted that project in Codex, Codex loaded the project's `.codex/config.toml`, and any `[mcp_servers.*]` command declared there ran as you, outside the read-only reviewer sandbox, on every review. The reviewer now marks the project directory, its parents and its symlink-resolved path as untrusted, so only your own `~/.codex/config.toml` loads. An SDK loaded from `reviewer.agent.codexSdk.path` that is older than 0.163.0 (the lowest supported peer version) is now refused, since it would silently drop the override.

* fix(codex): keep the workspace's .codex/config.toml out of the reviewer by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/66

## What's Changed

### Replace the built-in review policy

`reviewer.instructions` could only add to the built-in policy, which leans toward asking a human (it escalates whenever the user's intent is unknown or the operation is ambiguous). The new `reviewer.replaceDefaultPolicy` option makes your instructions the whole policy instead.

```jsonc
"reviewer": {
  "replaceDefaultPolicy": true,
  "instructions": [
    "Allow builds, tests, linters and type checks run through `pnpm` scripts.",
    "Escalate everything else, including package installs and `git push`."
  ]
}
```

- Drops the built-in allow/deny/escalate rules ("safe and within the user's intent", "if userIntent is null, escalate…") from the `agent` and `chat` prompts, and the `decision` backend's criteria are phrased against your policy. An operation your policy does not decide is escalated.
- Kept: the answer format, the review check, the untrusted-data guard and boundary, the conversation authorization rules, and `minAllowProbability`.
- Requires `reviewer.instructions`; the plugin fails at startup otherwise. The reviewer no longer checks that an operation matches your request, so set it only in configuration you trust.

* feat: add reviewer.replaceDefaultPolicy to replace the built-in review policy by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/65

### Reviewer sessions no longer clutter the session list (OpenCode V2)

On OpenCode V2, `agent` reviewer sessions are now linked to their originating session instead of appearing as top-level sessions. Set `reviewer.agent.cleanupSessions: true` to delete them after each decision (best-effort, never delays the verdict).

* fix: prevent reviewer sessions from cluttering chat history by @thisfilipe in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/51

## What's Changed

### Longer custom review instructions

`reviewer.instructions` was capped at 4,000 characters. The new `reviewer.maxInstructionsChars` option raises that cap (4,000–200,000; the default stays 4,000).

```jsonc
"reviewer": {
  "instructions": ["…a longer review policy…"],
  "maxInstructionsChars": 20000
}
```

- Instructions are sent, and billed, with every review and count toward each reviewer's size limit: `maxInputBytes` for the `agent` and `chat` reviewers, and `maxStateTokens` (or `longContext.maxStateTokens`) for the `decision` backend. Instructions that would fill a limit in use now make the plugin fail at startup instead of escalating every review.
- The `decision` backend now counts the instructions in its size estimate and in its check that the model read the whole prompt.
- Near the top of the range, raise `maxInputBytes` as well; with `longContext`, instructions larger than `maxStateTokens` send every review with long context.

* feat: let users raise the reviewer.instructions length limit by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/62

### Security hardening

- Prompts of subagent (child) sessions are no longer treated as user intent: a review uses the root session's latest prompt and conversation, and a new prompt in the root session cancels a subagent's pending allow. A failed or slow root lookup fails closed.
- The Codex SDK reviewer now runs with `approvalPolicy: "never"` in its read-only sandbox, so its automatic reviewer can no longer approve running outside the sandbox (this replaces the auto mode chosen for Codex in v0.8.0; the Claude Agent SDK reviewer is unchanged).
- The publish workflow verifies the release source before installing anything and installs and publishes with `--ignore-scripts`.

* fix: harden subagent user intent, Codex approvals and the publish workflow by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/58

### Dependencies

* ci(deps): bump jdx/mise-action from 5.1.2 to 5.2.1 in the all-actions group by @dependabot in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/59
* chore(deps): bump the all-dependencies group with 93 updates by @dependabot in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/60

## What's Changed

### Chat backend: OpenAI and Anthropic API keys

`reviewer.chat.provider` lets the `chat` backend call the OpenAI or Anthropic API directly with their own keys:

| `reviewer.chat.provider` | Endpoint | Key when `reviewer.chat.apiKey` is unset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"openai-compatible"` (default, unchanged) | `<baseURL>/chat/completions` | `AUTO_APPROVAL_CHAT_API_KEY` |
| `"openai"` | `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `"anthropic"` | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` (Messages API) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |

```jsonc
"reviewer": {
  "backend": "chat",
  "chat": { "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-haiku-5-5" }
}
```

- The vendor providers always call the vendor's own host and take no `baseURL`, so their key never reaches another server.
- The Anthropic provider uses the native Messages API (`x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `max_tokens: 16000`). Only a finished reply (`end_turn` / `stop_sequence`) is read for a verdict; a refusal or any other early stop fails the review, and "prompt is too long" or running out of context window counts as too large.
- Works for the decision backend's `onOversize: "chat"` fallback too.

* feat: call the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs from the chat backend by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/56
